name: Sculpture
summary: Sculpture majors create three-dimensional art using materials such as metal, wood, stone, clay, and found objects. The major teaches fabrication techniques alongside concepts of space, form, and installation.
description: Sculpture students learn a wide range of processes, including carving, modeling, mold-making and casting, welding and metal fabrication, woodworking, and increasingly digital fabrication with 3D printing and CNC machines. They also explore installation, site-specific work, public art, and performance. Safety training and shop skills are a significant part of the program. Critiques and courses in art history and theory help students develop a conceptual approach to their work. The major typically ends with a thesis exhibition. Graduates become exhibiting artists and public artists and also find work in fabrication shops, prop and exhibit building, and museums.
